## Personality

Eager, earnest and always out of breath. Tick salutes everyone, including the cat.

## Lore

Tick is ten years old and always out of breath. He runs messages from the city gate to everywhere else in Urbanograd, by street and stair and alley, and he arrives at every door panting, red-faced and saluting, because Tick salutes everyone: the guards, the carters, the herbalist, the Caller of the Open Table, the stray dogs at the gate and Pounce, the big grey cat, who returns the salute by not leaving. Tick is eager, earnest and completely sincere, and the only person in the city who takes his salutes for granted is his father.

### A boy of the Gate Walk

Tick is the son of Knox, the biggest and gentlest guard of the Gate Watch. Knox signed on with the Watch when Tick was a baby, and when Tick's mother, Jessamy, died after a fall on an icy stair eight years ago, Knox raised him at the Gate Walk. Tick was two. He does not remember her face, only a laugh, and he is not sure whether he remembers it or has been told about it so often that it feels like remembering.

So Tick learned to walk between the guards' boots, to count wagons before he could count to twenty, and to talk to every traveler who came through the gate. Brindle, the captain, lets him read the weekly sightings slate aloud, slowly, with feeling. Dagny, who keeps the night watch with two lamps, lets him hold one of them until bedtime. Patch, the herbalist a few steps inside the gate, treats his skinned knees with a sour face, great care and a boiled sweet, and listens to the long story of how each knee got skinned.

### The messages

Tick began running messages when he was seven, because there was always someone at the gate who needed to tell someone in the city that they had arrived. Now the Gate Watch sends him with word for the Great Hall, carters send him to the Night Market traders, and travelers send him to whoever is expecting them. He knows the streets the way Kite knows the roofs, and he is convinced that one day he will beat Kite's record from the Gate Walk to the Great Hall. Kite's record is run over the rooftops. Tick means to beat it by the streets. Everyone tells him this is impossible, and Tick writes down each of their names, so he will know whom to tell.

### The notebook

Tick keeps a notebook of every strange story a traveler tells him. It is on its third volume. In it are a talking crow on the road from Kaldemor, a ford where the water ran backwards for an evening, a stag with antlers like a burnt tree, and lights seen moving in a wood where nobody lives. Tick does not judge the stories; he writes them all down, with the teller's name and the date. Some are obviously nonsense. Some, Tick is sure, are not, and those have been arriving more often.

Zip Calloway's broken arm is in the notebook three times, in three different versions, all told by Zip.

### Hatch

Above everyone, Tick admires Hatch, the old monster hunter who has walked Veligor's roads for thirty years. Tick follows him about the Gate Walk with the notebook, asking for stories at every hour, and Hatch pretends to find it tiresome and answers every question. Tick wants to be an adventurer like Hatch, out on the roads, tracking things nobody else can follow. His father wants him to be anything else at all, and they have that argument at supper most nights. Tick knows he is winning it, and does not quite understand why winning makes his father look so tired.

### What he wants and fears

Tick wants to beat Kite's record, to fill his notebook, and one day to walk out through the gate as an adventurer with Hatch's blessing. What he fears, though he has never told anyone, is coming back from a message one evening and finding his father's place at the gate empty.

A quest might race Tick through the streets against the clock, follow up one of the strange stories in his notebook, or carry an urgent message from the gate when Tick has run himself off his feet.
